about: MUTATING — set the tags of ONE Longhorn disk a worker already has (infra/forge/longhorn-disk-tags.sh <node> <disk> <tags> <plan_sha256>) through the forge's ops_kubectl door (the admin kubeconfig David placed, infra/estate/ops-credentials.sh). Filed as backlog aa650aaf on 2026-11-12: design 3c475a19 places the system of record on w-3's u-postgres tagged durable,postgres, durable replicas on u-data durable, and tags every current default disk durable before car 4 selects with diskSelector [postgres]; on origin/main 6b2bd7c48 no door wrote a disk's tags (add-longhorn-disk always writes [], reregister-longhorn-disk re-adds the tags it found). AUTHORISED PER RUN BY DAVID'S PASSKEY in design 17835005's shape, as the longhorn-disk family is: it declares requires_approval with the read-only plan-a-longhorn-disk-tags (this script's --plan) as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders and patches nothing unless today's plan hashes to it. The node's disks before are in the bytes, and a disk that already carries the tags is refused, so a second run of an applied plan is refused: at most once. THE BOUND IS THE SCRIPT'S, NEVER A PARAM: a registry node whose role is talos-worker, with the cluster agreeing on its address and carrying no control-plane label (refused before any door opens, as every mutating node verb but node-converge is); a disk already in the node's spec.disks, named u-<volume> at exactly /var/mnt/<volume> or the node's ONE default-disk-<hex> at exactly /var/lib/longhorn; tags spelled exactly as one of the script's ADMITTED_TAGS — durable, durable,postgres, scratch, or none (design 3c475a19's words, and the untagged disk add-longhorn-disk writes); Longhorn reading the node Ready=True and the disk Ready=True and Schedulable=True with a diskUUID; tags that differ from the disk's now; and no replica on the disk (by diskID, or by node and path) whose volume's diskSelector the new tags would no longer hold, since Longhorn moves nothing when tags change — or nothing is done (exit 78; a replica naming a volume the list does not hold is CANNOT ANSWER, exit 1). THE WRITE is one kubectl patch --type=json that TESTS spec.disks is still exactly the map the plan read and REPLACES spec.disks/<disk>/tags (ADDS it when the record has no tags key) — a compare-and-set; nothing is moved or deleted, no other field or disk is written. Tags narrow only volumes whose diskSelector names a tag; whether a volume with no diskSelector still places on the disk is Longhorn's allow-empty-disk-selector-volume, which the plan reads and carries in its signed bytes (unreadable is CANNOT ANSWER), and the plan says which for the passkey to read. THE EFFECT IS READ BACK: every 10 s for up to 300 s, the Longhorn node; only when spec.disks/<disk>/tags reads the planned tags, every other field of the disk and every other disk reads as the plan did, and Longhorn's own status for the disk still reads Ready=True and Schedulable=True under the plan's diskUUID is the effect line printed, and otherwise the run exits 1 saying the tags are NOT proven with what was read (the inverse is this verb again with the tags before). Timeout 720: the plan's reads again (up to ~300 s with a first image pull), the patch (20 s), and the script's own 300 s read-back, which gives its verdict before the runner's kill.
effect: ^set-longhorn-disk-tags: [a-z0-9-]+ has Longhorn disk (u-[a-z0-9-]+|default-disk-[0-9a-f]+) tagged [a-z,]+ — read back: Ready=True, Schedulable=True, diskUUID [0-9a-f-]+ \(unchanged\), and its [0-9]+ other disk\(s\) unchanged \(after [0-9]+s\)$
